messages:
jamie: Hey team — onboarding a new EU account (acct-redwood-eu3-ml) for a customer PoC. Need help with networking + quota asks before we flip traffic. TL;DR: large GPU fleet (H100 nodes), ENI/IPv4 headroom, PrivateLink to partner artifact store, and egress design to avoid massive NAT gateway costs.

eli: thanks — can you list the specific quota increases and subnet plan? Also any hard deadlines?

jamie: Deadline: customer wants test runs in 3 weeks. Requests: 1) EC2 quota for H100 family: 40 x hpc.g5dn-style (we're actually using a marketplace image that maps to h100-backed instance family) — AWS quota team usually needs exact instance family name, but we're framing as 40 GPU instances, preferred region eu-west-3. 2) VPC IPv4 CIDR: we need /18 for the infra subnets (enough IPs for 3 AZs, autoscaled k8s + ENIs). 3) Increase Elastic IP limit for the account from default 5 -> 40 (we plan a small pool for NAT failover tests). 4) ENI per-instance / ENI IP quota: our GPU AMIs use enhanced networking with 8+ secondary IPs each. Need to raise 'IP addresses per network interface' and 'Elastic network interfaces per region' if possible. 5) Create VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, STS) + a PrivateLink endpoint for partner (artifacts.partner.internal) — need guidance on PrivateLink partner onboarding (service name + VPC endpoint config).

ashley-eng: quick note: the GPU nodes will attach 3 elastic network interfaces each for the rostering sidecar, monitoring, and data-plane (SR-IOV). That explains the high ENI count per instance. Also we plan to use NodePort for legacy infra which eats IPs.

eli: For the NAT question: are you expecting per-AZ NAT gateways or centralized egress via a transit hub? Per-AZ NAT is easiest but will cost ~0.045 USD/hr per NAT gw plus data processing fees. If we route egress via central transit TGW, we can share fewer NATs but add cross-AZ data charges.

jamie: Good point. Prefer transit TGW to reduce the number of NATs, but customer rules require egress IP allowlist for partner services — that pushes us toward a small pool of stable EIPs behind a few NATs. Cost estimate: if we need 6 NAT gateways (prod/staging across 3 AZs) that's ~400 USD/month just for NAT gateway base. Trying to avoid that for PoC.

kevin-net: I can loop with our AWS TAM. For quota asks: best to open a single support case listing exact service quotas (EC2 On-Demand standard instances, EIP limit, ENI limit, VPC Elastic IPs, EBS gp3 IOPS if needed). I can prepare the account-level file. Also, PrivateLink: we need the partner's NLB service name (com.amazonaws.vpce.eu-west-3.vpce-svc-xxxx). Partner usually gives us that.

quota-bot: Automated note: Please include your AWS account ID and exact region in quota requests. See template: `aws support create-case --service-code \"general-inquiry\" --category-code \"quota-increase\" --language \"en\" --communication-body \"Request increase: EC2 GPU family: 40 h100-type instances in eu-west-3, EIPs: 40, ENIs per-region: 2000, IPs-per-ENI: 50. Account ID: 123456789012\"`

jamie: Adding account ID: 123456789012. Proposed subnet plan: one /18 (10.32.0.0/18) split into three /20s for k8s node pools (nodepool-az1/az2/az3), two /24s for infra services (bastion, logs), and /21 for shared services (SQS, redis-like). That leaves room for autoscaling. Thoughts?

sara_ops: /18 -> split across AZs works. One warning: AWS will assign ENI counts against subnet capacity for secondary IPs; with NodePort + sidecars we should reserve ~30% of IPs for buffer. For a /20 (~4096 addresses) that's ~2800 usable after AWS reservations; we should size accordingly. Also enable AWS VPC IPAM so we can manage pool expansion later.

ashley-eng: For PrivateLink onboarding, partner sent us `vpce-svc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h`. Kevin, can you engage them for a test endpoint? We need to validate DNS + TLS handshake.

kevin-net: will do. Also recommend we request 'Prefix Lists' usage to pin egress rules for partner allowlist instead of an ever-changing EIP set. Gives us easier firewall rules.

jamie: Action items from thread: 1) Kevin to open quota escalation with TAM + attach sample support CLI body (by EOD). 2) Eli/sara to confirm egress architecture (transit TGW vs per-AZ NAT) with cost calc — prefer 2 NATs behind TGW for PoC for stable EIPs. 3) Ashley to validate partner PrivateLink svc and share service name (they already posted ID above). 4) I'll submit the official subnet/CIDR plan and enable IPAM.

eli: I'll model cost tradeoffs quickly: TGW+2 NATs vs 6 NATs and post numbers here. If PoC approved, we'll schedule the quota request as high-priority.

jamie: Thanks all. If anyone has quick objections to the /18 choice speak up now. Otherwise I'll start the support case draft and attach the sample CLI from quota-bot. :thumbsup:

kevin-net: no objections from me. I'll ping our TAM and escalate once you drop the support case link.

quota-bot: Case created (automated): 1234567890 — AWS support will respond within 24–48 hours.

ashley-eng: noted. I'll start smoke tests for PrivateLink once endpoint is available.

eli: Keeping thread open until we see the quota approval. Update here when you get the support case link.

jamie: Link to draft support case attached: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home?region=eu-west-3#/case/?caseId=1234567890 — feel free to edit.
